annotations.description:
Annotations on the Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations.
The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k.
Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required),
separated by a slash (/).
Prefix must be a DNS subdomain.
Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics,
with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: annotations has no security impact on the service or data

bare_metal_version.description: A human readable description of this Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
bare_metal_version.rationale: Bare metal version is a critical security parameter that determines the version of the bare metal admin cluster and can affect compliance with security requirements.

description.description: A human readable description of this Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
description.rationale: Description has no security impact on the service or data

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The bare metal admin cluster name.
name.rationale: Display name has no security impact on the service or data

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project is not important enough to have security implications.

cluster_operations.description: Specifies the Admin Cluster's observability infrastructure.

cluster_operations.enable_application_lo.description: Whether collection of application logs/metrics should be enabled (in addition to system logs/metrics).
cluster_operations.enable_application_lo.rationale: enable_application_logs does not have security impact on the service.

control_plane.api_server_args.description:
Customizes the default API server args. Only a subset of
customized flags are supported. Please refer to the API server
documentation below to know the exact format:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kube-apiserver/

control_plane.api_server_args.argument.description: The argument name as it appears on the API Server command line please make sure to remove the leading dashes.
control_plane.api_server_args.argument.rationale: argument does not have security impact on the service.

control_plane.api_server_args.value.description: The value of the arg as it will be passed to the API Server command line.

control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.description: Configures the node pool running the control plane. If specified the corresponding NodePool will be created for the cluster's control plane. The NodePool will have the same name and namespace as the cluster.
The generic configuration for a node pool running the control plane.

The map of Kubernetes labels (key/value pairs) to be applied to
each node. These will added in addition to any default label(s)
that Kubernetes may apply to the node. In case of conflict in
label keys, the applied set may differ depending on the Kubernetes
version -- it's best to assume the behavior is undefined and
conflicts should be avoided. For more information, including usage
and the valid values, see:
  - http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/user-guide/labels.html
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs.
For example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX).
The list of machine addresses in the Bare Metal Node Pool.

version -- it's best to assume the behavior is undefined and
conflicts should be avoided. For more information, including usage
and the valid values, see:
  - http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/user-guide/labels.html

Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX). Possible values: ["EFFECT_UNSPECIFIED", "PREFER_NO_SCHEDULE", "NO_EXECUTE"]

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.description:
a list of non-overlapping IP pools used
by load balancer typed services.
The addresses that are part of this pool.

This avoids buggy consumer devices mistakenly
dropping IPv4 traffic for those special IP addresses.
If true, prevent IP addresses from being automatically assigned.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.description: BGP autonomous system number (ASN) of the cluster.
BGP autonomous system number (ASN) of the cluster.

The IP address of the control plane node that
connects to the external peer.

load_balancer.manual_lb_config.enabled.description: Whether manual load balancing is enabled.

load_balancer.port_config.control_plane_.description: The port that control plane hosted load balancers will listen on.
load_balancer.port_config.control_plane_.rationale: Sets the TCP port the control-plane load balancer listens on. A port number is an environment-specific value with no inherently 'secure' choice; constraining it would require hardcoding a port, which is overreaching and not a security archetype.

load_balancer.vip_config.description: Specified the Bare Metal Load Balancer Config

load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.description: The VIP which you previously set aside for the Kubernetes API of this Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.rationale: A virtual IP address the team sets aside for the Kubernetes API. It is an environment-specific network value; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target.

maintenance_config.maintenance_address_c.description:
All IPv4 address from these ranges will be placed into maintenance mode.
Nodes in maintenance mode will be cordoned and drained. When both of these
are true, the "baremetal.cluster.gke.io/maintenance" annotation will be set
on the node resource.
maintenance_config.maintenance_address_c.rationale: maintenance_address_cidr_blocks does not require specific security considerations.

network_config.advanced_networking.description: Enables the use of advanced Anthos networking features.

network_config.island_mode_cidr.pod_addr.description: All pods in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.island_mode_cidr.pod_addr.rationale: Pod address CIDR blocks are not important enough to have security implications.

network_config.island_mode_cidr.service_.description: All services in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.island_mode_cidr.service_.rationale: Service address CIDR blocks are not important enough to have security implications.

network_config.multiple_network_interfac.description:
When set network_config.advanced_networking is automatically
set to true.

node_access_config.description: Specifies the node access related settings for the bare metal user cluster.

node_access_config.login_user.description:
LoginUser is the user name used to access node machines.
It defaults to "root" if not set.
node_access_config.login_user.rationale: The OS username used to access node machines (defaults to root). It is an environment-specific operational value; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain which login account a team uses, so it is not a useful policy target.

node_config.max_pods_per_node.description:
The maximum number of pods a node can run. The size of the CIDR range
assigned to the node will be derived from this parameter.
node_config.max_pods_per_node.rationale: max_pods_per_node does not require specific security considerations.

proxy.no_proxy.description:
A list of IPs, hostnames, and domains that should skip the proxy.
For example: ["127.0.0.1", "example.com", ".corp", "localhost"].
proxy.no_proxy.rationale: no_proxy does not require specific security considerations.

proxy.uri.description:
Specifies the address of your proxy server.
For Example: http://domain
WARNING: Do not provide credentials in the format
of http://(username:password@)domain these will be rejected by the server.
proxy.uri.rationale: uri does not require specific security considerations.

security_config.description: Specifies the security related settings for the Bare Metal User Cluster.

security_config.authorization.description: Configures user access to the Bare Metal User cluster.

security_config.authorization.admin_user.description: Users that will be granted the cluster-admin role on the cluster, providing full access to the cluster.
The name of the user, e.g. 'my-gcp-id@gmail.com'.
security_config.authorization.admin_user.rationale: Names a principal granted cluster admin access. As an access-granting principal it is a valid policy target: enforce against public/wildcard principals so admin access is never granted broadly; the policy must not pin specific user identities.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.description:
Specifies the config for local PersistentVolumes backed
by mounted node disks. These disks need to be formatted and mounted by the
user, which can be done before or after cluster creation.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.storage_c.description: The StorageClass name that PVs will be created with.

storage.lvp_share_config.description:
Specifies the config for local PersistentVolumes backed by
subdirectories in a shared filesystem. These subdirectores are
automatically created during cluster creation.

storage.lvp_share_config.shared_path_pv_.description: The number of subdirectories to create under path.
storage.lvp_share_config.shared_path_pv_.rationale: shared_path_pv_count does not have security impact on the service.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.description: Defines the machine path and storage class for the LVP Share.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.stor.description: The StorageClass name that PVs will be created with.
